key_insight: PyraTok learns discrete video tokens at multiple spatiotemporal resolutions and explicitly aligns them with language, producing semantically structured latents that improve cross-modal alignment and zero‑shot transfer for video understanding and generation.
problem_solved: Existing video tokenizers use a single scale, small vocabularies, and weak language supervision, which leads to ambiguous, non-semantic tokens and poor text–video transfer and generation control.
method: Start from a pretrained video VAE and extract a pyramidal set of spatiotemporal latents (multiple resolutions/scales) instead of a single-scale codebook.
Learn discrete codebooks per scale and a hierarchical composition so tokens capture both coarse global semantics and fine local motion/appearance.
Align tokens with language via cross-modal supervision (e.g., contrastive and token-level grounding) so discrete latents become semantically meaningful and text-controllable.
impact: PyraTok produces more interpretable, language-aligned video tokens that improve zero-shot generalization, controllability and downstream performance for text-to-video generation and video understanding tasks, making multimodal pipelines more robust and scalable.
visual_elements: Pyramid diagram: video frames → multi-scale spatiotemporal token layers (coarse → fine) to show hierarchical latents.
Alignment schematic: arrows from tokens at each scale to text embeddings illustrating cross-modal supervision/contrastive grounding.
Pipeline flowchart: pretrained VAE → pyramidal tokenizer → language alignment → downstream uses (T2V, retrieval, understanding).
Comparison bar or radar chart (conceptual): single-scale tokenizer vs PyraTok on metrics like semantic alignment, zero-shot transfer, and controllability.
paper_title: PyraTok: Language-Aligned Pyramidal Tokenizer for Video Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Adheesh Juvekar, Kiet A. Nguyen, Dong-Hwan Jang
